thread.title: Alphabet: The Time Is Now - Alphabet, Inc. Cl C (NASDAQ:GOOG)

author: Michael Wiggins De Oliveira
title: Alphabet: The Time Is Now - Alphabet, Inc. Cl C (NASDAQ:GOOG)
text:
Investment Thesis Alphabet ( GOOGL )( GOOG ) continues to be undervalued . It won't remain a bargain forever. Alphabet's core operations continue to spit out strong cash flows, with plenty of upside coming from 'Google other revenues'; yet Alphabet's stock still trades at a bargain price .
Share Volatility The past 3 months have seen a lot of volatility in Alphabet's share price. Savvy investors would be wise to ignore this volatility. In fact, contrary to the common spiel of 'buy the dips', I actually argue that investors are much better off by buying Alphabet's shares and holding them for a few years rather than attempting to market time each dip .
Either the valuation makes sense or it doesn't. Waiting for this stock to sell off 5% to buy more shares makes little sense. Besides, this develops the wrong sort of temperament from the investor. For instance, an investor would not rush out to buy a house, just because it fell 5% in price - either the house's price makes sense or it doesn't . Same with buying shares in Alphabet. Either its valuation makes sense, and its present valuation carries enough margin of safety, or it doesn't .
Having strength in one's conviction to buy when the whole market is selling is difficult to do at the best of times, requiring great fortitude from the investor. Po ssibly more importantly, odds are that when the market does ultimately sell off, investors might not have capital at their disposal . Additionally, while one waits for the market to sell off, in the interim period, Alphabet's shares may have risen in price by a substantial amount . All in all, this whole affair of buying into dips, seems great to discuss in theory but terribly inadequate in practice .
Google Cloud Platform I am a firm believer that Alphabet's cloud platform could in time, become a significant revenue generator . Furthermore, according to CEO Pichai's own comments during Alphabet's Q2 2018 earnings call , he spoke out confidently of GCP's prospects highlighting how its cloud platform continues to pick up momentum . Obviously , one would expect to hear such comments from a leading tech CEO.
However , this sense conviction is firmly backed by Alphabet's results. Such that, in Alphabet's Q2 2018 10-Q , we can see how even without tangible numbers being reported , how Alphabet's other revenue line was up 36% YoY (this line accounts for roughly 14% of total revenue in Q2 2018), so it's a significant contributor to Alphabet total revenue .
Further, what is particularly noteworthy is how Alphabet reports the constituents of this business line (Google other revenues) in its 10-Q. Alphabet reports that,
[the] growth [in Google other revenues] was primarily driven by revenues from Google Cloud offerings , hardware sales, and revenues from Google Play
Thus, one can logically infer that the units are reported in order of largest contribution to growth . Also, given that CFO Porat highlighted on the call, that advertising investments in cloud increased, and lead to an increase of 27% in operating expenses (and outpaced revenue growth), this should reaffirm to investors that Alphabet is serious about its cloud business .
For now, demand for its cloud offering will only grow, as businesses become increasingly dependent on high-performing compute infrastructure . Additionally, in a show of confidence in its cloud prospects, Alphabet's increase in headcount continues to go towards its cloud operations - both technical and sales roles .
Nevertheless , at present GCP is only a very small player in the overall cloud wars, with its revenue unlikely to have an annual run rate significantly larger than $5 billion - making it one of the smallest players .
However , Alphabet has the distribution channel potential, as well as enough technical capabilities to mount a meaningful challenge to the sector, thus I reason it is only a matter of time until Alphabet's cloud revenue meaningfully builds upon this positive momentum .
However , the great thing about this slow start is that investors are not being asked to pay much for its shares, and in the event that Alphabet actually succeeds in taking market share in this sector, it will reap the rewards of this sector's strong secular tailwinds .

Superficially , it appears that Alphabet's cash flows are being valued at fair value. However , as we have discussed above, Alphabet's cloud prospects (not to mention revenue from other potential business lines, such as autonomous vehicles, under Waymo) offer patient investors plenty of upside potential .
However , unlike other tech stocks, at the moment, investors are not asked to pay up hardly anything for the event that Alphabet succeeds . Obviously , not all endeavors which Google has embarked on have been successful. Google’s inroads into mobile hardware sales have arguably been a flop by Alphabet’s high standards; having said that, for a lesser company, taking any market share from Apple’s ( AAPL ) stronghold in the smartphone market could certainly be classed as a success .
Moreover, compared with Amazon ( AMZN ), Alphabet is absolutely trading at a bargain valuation. Why is Amazon's valuation any sort of indication over Alphabet's potential intrinsic value? Because, in this author's opinion, Amazon gets a large proportion of its high valuation because of its cloud's prospects, AWS . Remember, AWS is Amazon's only high-profit margin segment.
Takeaway Although Alphabet has its upcoming earnings coming within two week's time, I argue that rather than trying to react to Alphabet's quarterly results and outlook at the time, I suggest that investors take this opportunity now to invest and forget trying to time the market, and stay invested for 2-3 years .
Alphabet is a phenomenal money-making machine, which has the track record of being innovative as well as, be competitively-minded . At the moment, Alphabet's valuation does not reflect much in the way of hope that Alphabet could triumph in taking significant market share in the cloud wars .
